cta.title: Want a tool that does this for you?
cta.body: Syncologic will help you move folders between cloud providers without downloading them first. You'll preview every change before anything happens, run the transfer, and finish with a clear report. Join the waitlist for early access.

items.a: Pricing isn't final, but the structure is set: a free tier (5 GB hosted per month plus unlimited browser-tab transfers), Pro around $9 a month for 500 GB hosted, Pro+ around $29 a month for 5 TB. Running on your own server stays free.
Early access is open now via the waitlist. Joining never bills you; moving onto a paid plan will always be an explicit step.

items.q: What happens if a transfer fails halfway?
items.a: It picks up where it stopped. Files already verified at the destination are skipped on retry; failed ones go back in the queue. The report tells you what happened and which retries fixed it.

items.q: What does the preview actually show me?
items.a: A list of every file that will be copied, replaced, or left alone, by name, size, and target path. Nothing moves until you confirm.
Yes. Every part that handles a transfer (runners, transfer logic, provider adapters) is published source-visible. You can read what runs on your data before you trust it.

items.q: Can I run it on my own server?
items.a: Yes. The Private Runner runs on any server, NAS, or VPS you control. Files never reach our infrastructure. Free during early access.

affects.title: What affects cost
affects.subtitle: Three factors shape what your plan should look like.

volume.title: Data volume
volume.body: The biggest single driver — how much data moves per job and per month.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.body: One-time migrations, recurring backups, and continuous sync each price differently.

runner.title: Where the transfer runs
runner.body: Only hosted transfers use our bandwidth and count against your monthly GB. Anything that runs in your browser, on your machine, or on your own server stays uncapped.

items.a: The plan structure is set. Exact prices may shift slightly before launch.

items.q: Will there be an annual plan with a discount?
items.a: Yes. We're planning an annual option at a discount; the exact pricing isn't set, and it'll launch alongside the paid plans — not before.

items.q: Will I be charged automatically when launch happens?
items.a: No. Joining the waitlist never bills you. Moving from waitlist to a paid plan is always an explicit step.

items.q: What if I move more data than my plan includes?
items.a: On Free, once you hit the 5 GB monthly cap, hosted transfers will stop until the next month — Browser Runner transfers will keep working. Pro and Pro+ will add 1 TB for $2.50 each time you go over. Self-hosting will have no GB cap at all; bytes will flow through your own server, on your bandwidth.

items.q: Will failed transfers count against my quota?
items.a: No. Any quota used by a failed transfer will be refunded automatically — you only pay for bytes that actually land at the destination. Transfers you cancel yourself are the exception: the bytes already moved before you cancelled stay counted.

Yes. Once the binary is built, running the Private Runner on your own hardware will cost us nothing. During early access, all of self-hosting will be free — and the core 'move files between clouds on my own server' will always stay free.

items.q: Will I be able to transfer files from my own computer?
items.a: Yes, in two ways. With the Browser Runner you'll be able to push files from your computer straight to any connected provider — but the tab has to stay open the whole time. The planned Local Helper is a thin background daemon you'll install on your machine so a local folder can act like any connected provider; once it's running, the tab can close and the transfer keeps going.

developers.title: Developers — automate cloud file transfers
developers.description: Move files between clouds with a typed HTTP API, a CLI, webhooks, and runners you can host yourself.
developers.heroHeadline: Move files between clouds with one API.
developers.heroSubheading: For agencies, SaaS teams, and internal tools that move files between cloud providers without writing the glue.
developers.audienceLabel: Built for agencies, SaaS engineering teams, platform groups, and internal tooling.
developers.apiBody: Create a job with a source, destination, runner, and optional schedule. The control plane validates, dispatches, and emits progress events.
developers.apiCaption: Sketch — final shape will land with the v1 API.
developers.oauthBody: Your users connect their cloud accounts to Syncologic, not to your app. You never store provider credentials. The control plane manages the OAuth lifecycle and hands out scoped, short-lived tokens to runners — your app authenticates with Syncologic via your API key and never sees a provider token.
developers.oauthCaption: Your app integrates the API; the OAuth boundary stays on our side.
developers.cliTitle: A CLI for scripts and CI
developers.cliBody: Same jobs, driven from a terminal or a CI runner. Useful for one-shot migrations and for backups owned by a script you can read in a code review.
developers.cliCaption: Planned. Behavior mirrors the API one-to-one.
developers.webhooksTitle: Webhooks for the events you care about
developers.webhooksBody: Subscribe to job lifecycle events and stream them into your queue, your dashboard, or your audit log. Payloads will be HMAC-signed.
developers.noSdkBody: We will not ship an official SDK before the API is stable. The OpenAPI spec will be public, so you can generate a typed client in any language you already use.

faq.q: When can I start using the API?
faq.a: With early access. Syncologic is API-first — our browser frontend uses the same API you would. Every plan (Free, Pro, Pro+) includes API access from day one.

faq.q: Will there be a free tier for developers?
faq.a: There's no special developer offer — everything you'd pay (or not pay) is in the current plans.

faq.q: Do you handle OAuth on behalf of my users?
faq.a: Yes — your app never holds a provider token.
Webhook payloads will be HMAC-signed with a per-workspace secret you control.

update.label: Why not at launch
update.title: Self-hosting won't ship on launch day — and that's intentional
update.intro: Early access is about proving the core engine. Self-hosting is a different kind of product layered on top, and we'd rather wait than ship it half-right.

reasons.title: The engine has to be right first
reasons.desc: Cloud-to-cloud transfers need to be reliable, fast, and predictable before we bolt self-hosted runtime on top.

reasons.title: Self-hosting is a product, not a flag
reasons.desc: It's a two-plane product (control and data) running on hardware we don't control, with updates you trust us to ship. Security is our top priority, and on self-hosted infra it has to live inside the product itself.

reasons.title: It's a top post-launch priority
reasons.desc: Once the core is stable, self-hosting moves to the front of the roadmap.

howItWorks.title: How it works for you
howItWorks.intro: You run the transfer on your own server. We coordinate the job; the bytes never reach us. We call this setup a Private Runner.

filesStay.title: Files never park on our servers
filesStay.desc: Bytes travel from the source cloud, through your server, to the destination cloud. Our infrastructure never sees the files.

credentials.title: Your credentials stay with you
credentials.desc: Provider tokens live where your runner runs. We never receive them.

noInbound.title: No incoming connections to open
noInbound.desc: Your server reaches out to us. No firewall holes, no exposed services, no port-forwarding.

sourceVisible.title: Why code stays public
sourceVisible.body: Security comes from what you can verify, not what we promise. Every runner — Cloud Runner, Browser Runner, Local Helper, Private Runner — ships with source visible on GitHub, alongside the transfer logic and provider adapters. Read it, audit how credentials are handled, see how bytes move between providers, and decide whether to trust the system before a single file gets touched.

meta.title: Privacy — Syncologic
meta.description: How Syncologic collects, stores, and uses the email and segmentation answers you give when you join the waitlist.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Syncologic is pre-launch. The only personal data we collect right now is what you give us when you join the waitlist: your email and the segmentation answers you choose. This page tells you exactly what we keep, why, where, for how long, and how to remove it.

body.p: When you join the waitlist:

list: The segmentation answers you pick (use case, source provider, destination provider, estimated size, transfer frequency, preferred runner, role).
Your language and the page you joined from.
A non-reversible hash of your IP address. We use it for rate limiting and never store the original.
Your browser's user agent and referrer header, used for spam-pattern analysis.

body.p: We do not collect names, phone numbers, addresses, or payment details. There is no product to sign in to yet.
Three reasons:

list: To email you when Syncologic launches and at significant milestones.
To validate which use cases and provider pairs people actually want, so we build the right things first.
To prevent spam and abuse of the waitlist form.

body.p: We do not sell, share, or trade the list.
Email and segmentation answers live in a Supabase Postgres database with row-level security enabled. Access is limited to a service-role key held only by the Syncologic marketing-site backend.
Email delivery for waitlist confirmations and milestone updates goes through Resend. Resend retains delivery metadata (recipient, timestamp, status) per its own privacy policy.
Rate-limit counters, keyed by your hashed IP, live in Upstash Redis with a short TTL (24 hours).
Pageview counts and aggregate visitor data come from cookieless analytics — no tracking across sites, no per-visitor profile.
Supabase, Resend, and Upstash are based in the United States, where your data is processed.
Until launch plus six months, or until you unsubscribe — whichever comes first.
Hashed-IP rate-limit counters expire automatically (24 hours).
After unsubscribe, your row is marked as removed. We retain the hashed unsubscribe token for 30 days to prevent stale-link abuse, then delete the row entirely.
You can:

list: Ask what we have on you.
Have it ported to another service in a portable format.

body.p: Email hello@syncologic.com from the address on the list. We respond within 30 days.
You can also unsubscribe immediately yourself with the link at the bottom of any email we send.

Your consent for email and segmentation processing can be withdrawn at any time. The unsubscribe link in any email we send is the fastest way; emailing hello@syncologic.com works too. Withdrawing consent does not affect processing that already happened legally before the withdrawal.
Providing your email and segmentation answers is voluntary. If you do not, you simply do not get added to the waitlist — no other consequence.

We do not use automated decision-making or profiling that produces legal or significant effects on you. The segmentation answers are used only to prioritize what we build, not to make decisions about you individually.
We share the data above with:
We do not use Google Analytics, Meta Pixel, advertising trackers, or session-replay tools.
The site does not set tracking cookies.
Email hello@syncologic.com for any privacy question, data request, or concern. The site lives at syncologic.com.
